memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "Then the priest is to take one of the male lambs and offer it as a guilt offering, along with the log of oil; he shall wave them before the LORD as a wave offering. He is to slaughter the lamb in the sanctuary area where the sin offering and the burnt offering are slaughtered. Like the sin offering, the guilt offering belongs to the priest; it is most holy." - Lev 14:12-13 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
A guilt offering. That may puzzle us. This person was ill, not wicked. Why would healing require an offering for guilt?

Be careful here — the text does not say the disease was caused by sin. Job's friends made that mistake, and God rebuked them. Jesus was asked point-blank whether a blind man's condition was caused by his sin or his parents', and He answered: neither (John 9:1-3).

What this offering acknowledges is something broader. This person had been cut off from worship for a long season. Offerings unmade, festivals missed, tabernacle unvisited. And beyond that, all of us come before God as people who fall short — not because of any one illness, but because of who we are.

Notice where the lamb is slaughtered: in the same place as the sin offering and the burnt offering. The holiest ground. And notice the word applied to it: most holy.

There is a great dignity here. The person who had been called unclean, avoided, sent outside — their offering is handled on the most sacred ground in Israel, and called most holy.

That is what God does with those He restores. He does not bring us back to the edges. He brings us right into the centre.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Do you assume your suffering is God's punishment? What does John 9 say?
2. What does it mean that God brings you to the centre, not the margins?
3. Where do you still see yourself as second-class in God's household?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, thank You that You do not restore me to the edges but bring me into the centre of Your family. Free me from the lie that I am second-class in Your house. Amen.
